scalars.scalar_value: Minimum 1 year of related experience or training working in a biological or biomedical research laboratory

items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree in biology, molecular biology, genetics, biochemistry, or a related field, and/or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Minimum 1 year of related experience or training working in a biological or biomedical research laboratory
Experience with mammalian cell culture and/or CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing
Experience with molecular cloning, PCR-based genotyping, RT-PCR, and/or Western blotting.
Experience preparing cells or nuclei for genomic or single-cell experiments.

Under the supervision of the Principal Investigator, the Staff Research Associate 1 (SRA 1) will support ongoing research projects involving mammalian cell culture, genome editing, and single-cell genomic approaches. The SRA 1 will be responsible for routine preparation and maintenance of mammalian cell lines and will perform CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing. They will have the opportunity to learn and perform replication-timing labeling experiments and will assist with nuclei isolation from mammalian cell cultures for single-cell experiments. Additional responsibilities include maintaining inventories of reagents, cell lines, and samples used in single-cell experiments and supporting general laboratory operations. Experience with molecular cloning, PCR-based genotyping, RT-PCR, and Western blotting is preferred. Training will be provided for specialized techniques as appropriate.
This is a limited appointment that may convert to career.
Ability to follow established laboratory protocols and perform research procedures accurately and reproducibly.
Ability to maintain accurate, organized, and timely laboratory records and sample documentation.
Knowledge of basic molecular and cell biology principles and laboratory practices.
Ability to work safely with biological and chemical materials and follow laboratory safety procedures.
Ability to organize work, manage multiple routine tasks, and meet experimental timelines.
Ability to communicate effectively and work collaboratively in a research laboratory environment.
Skill in mammalian cell culture and aseptic technique.
Skill in RNA analysis, including RT-PCR.
Skill in protein analysis, including Western blotting.
Basic computer skills for data organization, documentation, and analysis.
